sudan.content: مطالبات بوضع المواطنين السودانيين في صميم عملية الإصلاح الأمني والعسكري - سودان تربيون تخطى الى المحتوى من نحن اتصل بنا English الجمعة , 23 أكتوبر - 2026 سودان تربيون أخبار السودان وتقارير حصرية لحظة بلحظة الرئيسية سياسة الأخبار تقصي الحقائق اقتصاد دولي اقاليم الرأي English سودان تربيون أخبار السودان وتقارير حصرية لحظة بلحظة الرئيسية اختيار المحرر مطالبات بوضع المواطنين السودانيين في صميم عملية الإصلاح الأمني والعسكري اختيار المحرر مطالبات بوضع المواطنين السودانيين في صميم عملية الإصلاح الأمني والعسكري 23 أكتوبر 2026 في اختيار المحرر , الأخبار , الانتقال الديمقراطي , الحرب بين الجيش السوداني والدعم السريع , السلام , السودان , سياسة , شؤون عسكرية 0 مطالبات بوضع المواطنين السودانيين في صميم عملية الإصلاح الأمني والعسكري الخرطوم، 23 أكتوبر 2026 – طالب المشاركون في المنتدى الرابع لـ«نداء سلام السودان» بوضع المواطنين في صميم عملية إصلاح القطاع الأمني والعسكري، وإخضاع المؤسسات العسكرية والشرطية والأمنية للرقابة المدنية وسيادة القانون. وتُعد قضية إصلاح القطاع الأمني والعسكري من أبرز الملفات المرتبطة بإنهاء الحرب في السودان، في ظل تعدد التشكيلات المسلحة وتعثر جهود توحيد القوات النظامية تحت قيادة مهنية واحدة وخاضعة للسلطة المدنية. وظل إصلاح المؤسسة العسكرية والأمنية أحد الملفات الخلافية خلال الفترة الانتقالية التي أعقبت سقوط نظام الرئيس عمر البشير في أبريل 2019، لا سيما فيما يتعلق بدمج قوات الدعم السريع في الجيش، وترتيبات القيادة والسيطرة، ودور المؤسسات العسكرية في الحياة السياسية والاقتصادية. وأكد المشاركون في المنتدى عبر ندوة أونلاين أن وقف الحرب وحماية المدنيين يرتبطان بمستقبل القطاع الأمني، بما يشمل ترتيبات التهدئة وانتشار القوات وحماية المدن، ومنع تشكيل مجموعات مسلحة جديدة، إلى جانب معالجة قضايا دمج القوات وتسريحها والمساءلة والعدالة الانتقالية. كما ناقش المشاركون ضرورة الفصل بين الحقوق المهنية لأفراد القوات النظامية، بما في ذلك الأجور والسكن والاستقرار الوظيفي، ومصالح القيادات المرتبطة بالاحتفاظ بالسلطة أو النفوذ الاقتصادي أو الإفلات من المساءلة عن الجرائم. وأشار النقاش إلى أن تعثر الاتفاقات السابقة لم يكن بالضرورة بسبب غياب المبادئ المتفق عليها، وإنما ارتبط بضعف آليات التنفيذ والرقابة ومحدودية القدرات الفنية اللازمة لضمان خضوع المؤسسات العسكرية للسلطة المدنية. وأوضحوا أن العمل سيشمل إتاحة البيانات اللازمة للإجابة عن تساؤلات تتعلق بآليات دمج القوات وتسريحها، وتهيئة بيئة آمنة تضمن حماية المواطنين خلال المرحلة الانتقالية. وشدد المشاركون، خلال المنتدى الذي استند إلى دراسة تناولت تصورات السودانيين وخبرات مدنية وسياسية وعسكرية وشرطية، على ضرورة توسيع النقاش بشأن إصلاح القطاع الأمني ليتجاوز مستقبل الجيش إلى قضايا طبيعة الدولة وسلطة استخدام القوة، ودور المؤسسات الأمنية في حماية المواطنين. وفي ختام المنتدى، أعلن المنظمون عدم اعتماد نموذج نهائي أو خطة محددة لإصلاح القطاع الأمني في المرحلة الحالية، مؤكدين مواصلة مراجعة المخرجات التحليلية وتطويرها تمهيداً لإعداد ورقة استراتيجية. مقالات ذات صلة الخارجية : لن نقبل الإنسان فولكر تورك بشدة تصعيد ضربات الطائرات المُسيّرة في أنحاء السودان خلال هذا الشهر، وعواقبها المدمرة على المدنيين في كردفان، ودارفور، والنيل الأزرق، والخرطوم، وولايات أخرى. وقد وثقت مفوضية الأمم المتحدة لحقوق الإنسان - خلال الأسابيع الثلاثة الأولى من الشهر الحالي - مقتل ما لا يقل عن 306 أشخاص وإصابة المئات جراء هجمات الطائرات المسيرة. وقالت في بيان صحفي إن الضربات "التي تنُسب إلى كل من القوات المسلحة السودانية وقوات الدعم السريع" طالت الأعيان المدنية والبنية التحتية، بما في ذلك المنازل والأسواق والمستشفيات ومواقع النزوح ومحطات توليد الكهرباء ومصادر المياه. وقال فولكر تورك: "إن الاستخدام المتزايد للطائرات المسيرة، التي تسببت بالفعل في غالبية الوفيات في صفوف المدنيين الناجمة عن النزاع في السودان هذا العام، أمر يثير قلقا بالغا ويُخلف خسائر بشرية مروعة". وجدد دعوة أطراف النزاع لاحترام واجباتها الواضحة والملزمة بموجب القانون الدولي الإنساني، بما في ذلك الامتناع عن توجيه الهجمات ضد المدنيين والأعيان المدنية. وقالت المفوضية إنها وثقت "في سياق يثير القلق" العديد من الهجمات بالمسيرات على مواقع النزوح، التي تؤوي أشخاصا سبق أن أُجبروا على الفرار من القتال. وقد أدت هذه الهجمات إلى ارتفاع حاد في أعداد الضحايا في صفوف النازحين. وفي الفترة بين 6 و10 تشرين الأول/أكتوبر، أسفرت هجمات بمُسيرات تنسب إلى القوات المسلحة السودانية على مراكز إيواء النازحين في مدينتي غبيش والنهود بولاية غرب كردفان، عن مقتل ما لا يقل عن 25 مدنيا وإصابة 31 آخرين، من بينهم نساء وأطفال. وفي أبو شندي بولاية النيل الأزرق، استهدفت طائرة مسيرة يُزعم أنها تابعة لقوات الدعم السريع، في 9 تشرين الأول/أكتوبر، تجمعا للنازحين كانوا يعملون في التعدين الحرفي للذهب قرب أحد مواقع إيواء النازحين، مما أسفر عن مقتل ما لا يقل عن 31 شخصا، معظمهم من النساء والأطفال. وفي 9 و16 تشرين الأول/أكتوبر، استهدفت طائرات مسيرة يزعم أنها لقوات الدعم السريع منطقة تعدين الذهب في منطقة باجون بمحلية قدير، بولاية جنوب كردفان، مما أسفر عن مقتل 42 مدنيا وإصابة 25 آخرين. وقالت المفوضية الأممية إن الهجمات على مناطق تعدين الذهب تُعزى الى دور اقتصاد الحرب في إدامة النزاع، كما تثير مخاوف جدية بشأن الاستهداف المتعمد لمواقع ذات قيمة اقتصادية للطرف الآخر في النزاع. ووفقا لقوانين الحرب، كما قالت المفوضية، فإن " مساهمة الأعيان في تمويل المجهود الحربي لا يكفي بحد ذاته لاعتبارها هدفا عسكريا". وذكرت مفوضية حقوق الإنسان أن " الضربات الانتقامية تبرز كاتجاه ناشئ يثير القلق" ، مع تنفيذ طائرات مسيرة نُسبت إلى قوات الدعم السريع هجمات على الخرطوم، بما في ذلك منطقة المطار، يُفاد بأنها جاءت ردا على غارات جوية يزعم تنفيذها من قبل القوات المسلحة السودانية على مدينة نيالا بولاية جنوب دارفور. مفوض حقوق الإنسان فولكر تورك شدد على ضرورة أن تتصدى جهود السلام "للتدفق المستمر للأسلحة الذي يؤجج النزاع، وأن تضغط من أجل وقف نقل الأسلحة التي تستخدم في تجاهل صارخ لالتزامات القانون الدولي الإنساني التي تهدف إلى حماية المدنيين". وشدد تورك على ضرورة اتخاذ خطوات نحو التوصل إلى وقف لإطلاق النار. وقال إن التوصل إلى تسوية بالتفاوض - تكون حقوق الإنسان في صلبها، وتستند إلى المساءلة عن الانتهاكات والتجاوزات واسعة النطاق التي ترتكب حاليا - هو السبيل الوحيد القابل للتحقيق نحو سلام مستدام في السودان. ♦ تحميل تطبيق أخبار الأمم المتحدة بالعربية من متجر آبل لأجهزة الأيفون والآيباد IOS أو من متجر غوغل لأجهزة أندرويد Android . ♦ الاشتراك في إشعارات البريد الإلكتروني. قصص ذات صلة مفوض حقوق الإنسان يحذر من اتساع نطاق النزاع في السودان في ظل تزايد استخدام والميليشيات المهندس وليد الخريجي نائب وزير الخارجية السعودي خلال مشاركته في الاجتماع الذي استضافته جنيف الأربعاء (واس) أكّدت السعودية أنه لا يمكن المساواة بين الحكومة السودانية ومجلس السيادة، وبين ميليشيات ارتكبت جرائم بحق الشعب السوداني، مُجدِّدة الرفض للكيانات الموازية والإجراءات غير المشروعة خارج المؤسسات الرسمية التي تمس وحدة السودان ولا تُعبِّر عن إرادة شعبه. جاء ذلك في كلمة ألقاها المهندس وليد الخريجي نائب وزير الخارجية السعودي، خلال الاجتماع التشاوري السادس بشأن تعزيز تنسيق مبادرات وجهود السلام في السودان، حيث شدَّد على جهود المملكة لوقف إطلاق النار وصون الوحدة والحفاظ على مؤسسات الدولة السودانية وحمايتها من الانهيار. وأوضح الخريجي أن هذه الجهود تستند إلى إعلان جدة للالتزام بحماية المدنيين الموقّع 11 مايو (أيار) 2023، واتفاقية وقف إطلاق النار قصير الأمد، مبيناً أن السعودية تدعم مبادرة المجموعة الخماسية وغيرها من الجهود الإقليمية والدولية للوصول لحل سياسي يحفظ سيادة السودان ووحدته وسلامته أراضيه. وأكد نائب وزير الخارجية أهمية مساندة الحكومة السودانية في جهودها لتهيئة حوار سوداني - سوداني داخل البلاد، مُشدِّداً على مواصلة المملكة العمل من أجل إنهاء الحرب واستعادة الاستقرار في السودان. جانب من الاجتماع التشاوري بشأن تعزيز تنسيق مبادرات وجهود السلام في السودان (الخارجية السعودية) وبيَّن الخريجي أن السعودية أعلنت تقديم 100 مليون دولار لتخفيف معاناة الشعب السوداني، وأطلقت حملة شعبية عبر منصة «ساهم»، حيث تجاوز إجمالي المساعدات السعودية للسودان 3.2 مليار دولار، فضلاً عن دعم إضافي بقيمة 145 مليون دولار. وأضاف أن هذه المساعدات تأتي في إطار خطة الاستجابة الإنسانية في السودان لعام 2026 خلال مشاركتها اجتماع تنسيق العمل الإنساني بشأن أزمة السودان، في برلين بتاريخ 15 أبريل (نيسان) 2026. من جانب آخر، التقى المهندس الخريجي، على هامش الاجتماع، وزيري الخارجية السويسري ألكسندر فازل، والنرويجي أندريس كرافيك، والشيخ شخبوط بن نهيان وزير الدولة بالخارجية الإماراتية، ومسعد بولس كبير مستشاري الرئيس الأميركي للشؤون العربية والأفريقية، كل على حدة. وجرى خلال اللقاءات الثنائية استعراض العلاقات الثنائية بين السعودية وبلدانهم، وآفاق التعاون المشترك، وناقشا الجهود الرامية لتعزيز الأمن والسلام في السودان والجهود المبذولة بشأنها، فضلاً عن المستجدات الإقليمية والدولية. مواضيع أخبار السعودية أخبار السودان السعودية الخليج العربي السودان العالم العربي العالم الأكثر قراءة Adel Abdelrheem 23 أكتوبر 2026 • تحديث : 23 أكتوبر 2026 الأرشيف SUDAN الخرطوم/ عادل عبد الرحيم/ الأناضول نفت الحكومة السودانية، الجمعة، صلة الجيش بهجوم بطائرة مسيرة استهدف سوق النعام في منطقة أبيي المتنازع عليها مع جنوب السودان، وأسفر عن مقتل 153 شخصا، بحسب حصيلة أعلنتها السلطات المحلية. والأربعاء، أعلن وزير الإعلام المكلف في إدارة منطقة أبيي التابعة لجنوب السودان، يوحنا أكول نقور، ارتفاع حصيلة قتلى هجوم بمسيرة استهدف سوق أميت، المعروف محليا بسوق النعام، إلى 153 شخصا، مقارنة بحصيلة سابقة بلغت 73 قتيلا. وقالت وزارة الخارجية السودانية، في بيان، إنه "لا توجد أي صلة للقوات المسلحة السودانية بهذه الحادثة المؤسفة"، معربة عن بالغ أسف الحكومة لسقوط ضحايا مدنيين في الهجوم. وأضافت أن الحكومة السودانية تجدد تضامنها مع أسر الضحايا، وتمنياتها للجرحى بالشفاء العاجل. واعتبرت الوزارة أن الحادثة "تشبه الجرائم التي ما زالت المليشيا الإرهابية تستمر في ارتكابها"، في إشارة إلى قوات الدعم السريع. ولفتت إلى هجوم استهدف مقر قوة الأمم المتحدة الأمنية المؤقتة لأبيي (يونيسفا) في مدينة كادوقلي جنوبي السودان، في 13 ديسمبر/ كانون الأول 2025، ما أدى إلى مقتل عدد من قوات حفظ السلام من الكتيبة البنغلاديشية آنذاك، فضلا عن استهداف قوافل مساعدات إنسانية. وفي اليوم ذاته، أعلن الجيش السوداني مقتل 6 أشخاص وإصابة 7 آخرين من أفراد بعثة الأمم المتحدة، في هجوم بثلاثة صواريخ أطلقتها مسيرة اتهم قوات الدعم السريع بتنفيذه ضد مقر البعثة في كادوقلي. في المقابل، نفت قوات الدعم السريع مسؤوليتها عن الهجوم. والاثنين، استدعت وزارة خارجية جنوب السودان السفير السوداني لدى جوبا، عصام كرار، احتجاجا على الهجوم الذي استهدف سوق أمييت في منطقة أبيي، وأسفر عن سقوط قتلى وجرحى من المدنيين. والخميس، أعلنت الأمم المتحدة مقتل 80 شخصا على الأقل وإصابة 27 آخرين في الهجوم، مشيرة إلى أنها لم تتمكن بعد من تحديد الجهة المسؤولة عنه. وتعد "أبيي" منطقة غنية بالنفط ومتنازعا عليها بين السودان وجنوب السودان، وحصلت على وضع إداري خاص بموجب اتفاقية السلام الشامل الموقعة في 9 يناير/ كانون الثاني 2005. وتعد المنطقة جسرا بين شمالي السودان وجنوبه، حيث تسكن في الشمال قبائل "المسيرية" العربية، أما جنوبا فتستوطن قبائل "الدينكا" الإفريقية. ويأتي الهجوم في ظل استمرار الحرب بالسودان بين الجيش وقوات الدعم السريع منذ أبريل/ نيسان 2023، على خلفية خلاف بشأن دمج الأخيرة في المؤسسة العسكرية. وأسفرت الحرب عن مقتل عشرات الآلاف ونزوح نحو 13 مليون شخص، By Publishing Desk Published 23 Oct 2026, 18:08 GMT 2 min read Share Share Copy link Add 3News as your preferred source on Google Preferred source Article tools Ask AI Listen to this article AI narration Playback position 0:00 1:42 10 10 Playback speed 1× President John Dramani Mahama arrived in the historic city of Gondar, Ethiopia, on Friday, October 23 for an official visit at the invitation of Ethiopian Prime Minister H.E. Dr Abiy Ahmed Ali. The visit comes ahead of the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Security in Africa, to be held in Bahir Dar. Shortly after arriving at Gondar Airport, President Mahama joined the Prime Minister to switch on the Megech Irrigation Development Project, a massive dam-and-reservoir infrastructure designed to transform agriculture and water supply in the region. The ambitious project, which began 18 years ago, stalled until Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali revived it three years ago and completed it. Spanning 870 hectares with a storage capacity of 185 million cubic metres, the Megech Dam is set to have a profound socio-economic impact. It will support irrigation of 17,000 hectares of agricultural land, significantly bolstering food security and productivity. In addition, the facility will provide a reliable supply of clean, potable water to the city of Gondar and its surrounding satellite towns. President Mahama commended the Government and people of Ethiopia for their resilience and dedication in delivering a transformative project that will serve generations to come. President Mahama will travel to Bahir Dar on Saturday to chair the 12th Tana High-Level Forum, where African leaders, policymakers, and security experts will discuss pressing peace, governance, and security challenges across the continent. ethiopia.content: PM Advisor Getachew Underscores Ethiopia’s Pivotal Geopolitical Position - ENA English - ENA Skip to Content PM Advisor Getachew Underscores Ethiopia’s Pivotal Geopolitical Position - ENA English Live: አማርኛ ትግርኛ Afaan Oromoo Af‑Soomaali Qafar Afa English Français عربي Politics Social Economy Sport Technology Environment Feature Videos About Us PM Advisor Getachew Underscores Ethiopia’s Pivotal Geopolitical Position 🔇Unmute Addis Ababa, October 23, 2026 (ENA) — A dvisor to the Prime Minister on East African Affairs, Getachew Reda emphasized Ethiopia’s pivotal geopolitical position, stressing that whatever political, economic, and security developments in the country carry serious implications for the wider region. The remarks came during the Tana Forum 2026 Special Envoys Dialogue, convened today in the city of Bahir Dar to address pressing regional security challenges in the Horn of Africa and the Red Sea region. The panelists included Advisor to the Prime Minister on East African Affairs Getachew Reda; UN Secretary-General’s Special Envoy for the Horn of Africa Guang Cong; French Special Envoy for the Horn of Africa Frédéric Clavier; Germany’s Special Envoy for the Horn of Africa, Ambassador Heiko Nitzschke; and Personal Envoy of the UN Secretary-General for Sudan, Pekka Haavisto. Speaking at the dialogue, Getachew underscored that whatever political, economic, and security developments unfold in Ethiopia carry profound ramifications for the broader Horn of Africa and Red Sea region. “Ethiopia is too important, and whatever developments happen in Ethiopia will have serious ramifications politically, economically, and in terms of security for the rest of the region,” Getachew said. Highlighting the nation’s status as a country of over 130 million people with one of the world’s fastest-growing economies, he noted that Ethiopia serves not only as an economic powerhouse but also as a critical contributor to international peace and security. He stressed that, as a neighbor to some of the region’s most volatile areas, Ethiopia’s responsibility in maintaining stability becomes even more vital. Addressing internal security dynamics, Getachew underscored the Ethiopian government’s commitment to resolving conflicts through peaceful dialogue and multilateral frameworks. “One thing we should take into account, in terms of addressing internal problems in Ethiopia, is the government's focus on addressing conflicts or possible sources of conflicts peacefully through dialogue,” he stated, referencing efforts to resolve the conflict in northern Ethiopia through the signing of the Pretoria Agreement. However, he cautioned that domestic efforts to achieve peace face serious external obstacles, pointing to interference from regional actors. Getachew singled out Eritrea as one of players of displaying “recalcitrant behavior” and continuing to “foment crisis” in the region. He urged the international community to adopt a holistic approach that distinguishes between internal peace initiatives and the necessity of confronting external forces fueling instability across the Horn, including in neighboring Sudan and Somalia. Highlighting how security challenges across the Horn of Africa, the Red Sea, and the Gulf are increasingly merging into a complex regional dynamic, UN Special Envoy Guang Cong described the current situation as a “polycrisis,” noting that ongoing conflicts in Sudan, South Sudan, and Somalia, alongside maritime threats in the Red Sea, are deeply interconnected. He emphasized that resolving these crises requires a coordinated regional approach rather than isolated measures. Echoing these concerns, German Special Envoy Ambassador Heiko Nitzschke noted the heightened sense of urgency among European and African policymakers in addressing these overlapping security threats, particularly given their impact on global trade routes through the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait. He underscored the need for region-led peace initiatives and economic integration. Pekka Haavisto, Personal Envoy of the UN Secretary-General for Sudan, also noted that international and regional diplomatic efforts must align to address complex, multi-state crises in the Horn of Africa. For his part, French Special Envoy for the Horn of Africa Frédéric Clavier emphasized that stronger multilateral cooperation is necessary to stabilize the broader Horn of Africa and Red Sea region. Moreover, the panelists highlighted key cross-border infrastructure, trade, and connectivity developments that reflect a shared commitment to long-term regional integration and stability. © Ethiopian News Agency 2023 Hidden

The dam, with a storage capacity of 185 million cubic metres, is expected to irrigate more than 17,000 hectares of farmland, directly benefiting tens of thousands of farmers, Abiy said in a statement posted on X. "Today, we officially inaugurated the Megech Irrigation Dam Project, a major milestone for historic Gondar and its surrounding community," Abiy said. The prime minister said the project had faced years of delays and implementation challenges before the government resolved obstacles to its completion through its Medemer development philosophy. Speaking at the inauguration of the Megech Irrigation and Water Supply Project in Gondar, the Prime Minister emphasized that sustainable national progress depends on strengthening local expertise and reducing reliance on external entities. Located on the Megech River, a major tributary of Lake Tana in the North Gondar Zone of the Amhara Region, the project is designed to expand agricultural production, improve access to clean drinking water and stimulate economic activity. With a storage capacity of 185 million cubic meters, the dam is expected to irrigate more than 17,000 hectares of farmland, benefiting tens of thousands of farmers. He cited the 19-year delay in completing the Megech project as an example of structural weaknesses that have hindered the timely delivery of public infrastructure. The Prime Minister identified delays and the accumulation of unfinished projects as major obstacles to national development, emphasizing the need to address the underlying institutional and administrative challenges. He also underscored the importance of effective coordination between federal and regional governments, saying stronger collaboration and aligned implementation efforts are necessary to achieve shared development objectives. PM Abiy further emphasized that development infrastructure belongs to the public and requires collective responsibility for its protection and proper use. Published 10 minutes ago on October 23, 2026 By Kulu Media News Desk Ethiopia's national security adviser Redwan Hussein addresses a regional security dialogue in Bahir Dar, calling for broader cooperation on Red Sea maritime security. Credit: ENA / via Kulu Media Ethiopia has called for a broader regional approach to Red Sea security, arguing that responsibility for protecting one of the world’s most important maritime trade routes should not rest exclusively with countries along its coastline. Redwan Hussein, Ethiopia’s national security adviser, made the remarks during a high-level dialogue in Bahir Dar focused on geopolitical changes, security challenges and international competition in the Horn of Africa and Red Sea region. Speaking to diplomats and other participants, Redwan warned that growing militarization, foreign power rivalries and renewed threats to commercial shipping were increasing instability across the region. He argued that Ethiopia, despite being landlocked, has a direct interest in maritime security because of its dependence on regional shipping routes for international trade. Ethiopia Seeks Wider Role in Red Sea Security Redwan said developments in the Red Sea have consequences extending far beyond the countries with direct coastlines. He pointed to the region’s strategic position linking the Red Sea, Arabian Peninsula, Indian Ocean and Mediterranean Sea, describing it as an essential gateway for international commerce. According to his remarks, the growing military presence in the Red Sea and threats to shipping have created security challenges requiring cooperation among regional governments and international partners. Redwan argued that responsibility for the waterway’s security should not be limited to a small group of coastal states. Instead, he called for collective action involving countries across the region and partners capable of contributing to maritime stability. The position reflects Ethiopia’s longstanding argument that its economic dependence on maritime trade gives it a significant stake in regional security arrangements. Although Ethiopia has no coastline, the country relies heavily on access to neighboring countries’ ports for international commerce. Redwan said Ethiopia has a responsibility to help prevent threats that could disrupt its trade and economic development. Shipping Threats and Regional Rivalries The national security adviser identified several factors contributing to instability across the Horn of Africa. These included historical grievances, disputes over resources, internal and cross-border conflicts, competition among foreign powers and the continuing threat of extremism. He also highlighted the strategic importance of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden. Threats to commercial shipping through the strait, alongside developments affecting the Strait of Hormuz, have increased concerns about the security of maritime trade routes, he said. Redwan warned that the militarization of the Red Sea and competition for influence could have consequences for countries throughout the Horn of Africa and beyond. The region’s natural resources, including critical minerals, agricultural land and water, also contribute to its geopolitical importance, according to his assessment. He argued that the combination of strategic geography, economic resources and political instability has exposed the Horn of Africa to sustained foreign influence and competition. Remarks Come Amid Ethiopia-Eritrea Tensions Redwan’s comments come at a particularly sensitive time for regional diplomacy. Relations between Ethiopia and Eritrea have deteriorated sharply, with the neighboring governments exchanging accusations over territorial security and support for armed groups. The confrontation has heightened international concern about the possibility of a broader regional conflict. Ethiopia has also repeatedly emphasized the importance of securing reliable maritime access. Earlier this month, President Taye Atske Selassie reaffirmed the government’s intention to pursue Red Sea access through diplomacy and mutually beneficial arrangements. The government’s maritime ambitions have become increasingly intertwined with its relations with neighboring countries, particularly Eritrea. However, Redwan’s speech focused on regional security cooperation and Ethiopia’s economic interests. He did not announce a new port agreement, military deployment or change in Ethiopia’s maritime access arrangements. His remarks should therefore be understood as a statement of Ethiopia’s security position rather than an announcement of a new operational policy. Call for Stronger Regional Cooperation Redwan also emphasized the need to strengthen cooperation between regional and continental organizations involved in peace and security. He said the Horn of Africa’s complex challenges require innovative approaches that address both immediate security threats and longer-term political and economic concerns. The national security adviser expressed hope that the dialogue among special envoys and regional stakeholders would produce practical recommendations capable of being translated into action. He also called for better coordination among existing peace initiatives and security frameworks. The discussions took place in Bahir Dar, where Ethiopia is hosting the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Security in Africa from October 23 to 25. The forum’s theme, Pathways to Peace in Africa: Economic Sovereignty and Geopolitical Transformation , reflects growing concern about the effects of international rivalries on African security and development. Redwan concluded by reaffirming Ethiopia’s commitment to regional peace, economic development and deeper integration. His remarks underline a central question facing governments around the Red Sea: how to balance the interests of coastal states with those of landlocked countries whose economies depend on secure maritime trade routes. Published 2 days ago on October 21, 2026 By Kulu Media News Desk Eritrean Foreign Minister Osman Saleh addresses the United Nations General Assembly in New York. (File photo: UN Photo) Eritrea has denied deploying troops inside Ethiopia and rejected international calls for both countries to exercise restraint, accusing the Ethiopian government of fueling regional instability amid escalating military and diplomatic tensions in the Horn of Africa. In a formal statement issued on October 21, 2026, Eritrea’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said its military forces remain entirely within the country’s internationally recognized borders and described Ethiopian allegations of an invasion as fabricated. The official statement , published by Eritrea’s Ministry of Information, presents Asmara’s position on the growing confrontation, including disputed borders, military deployments, territorial sovereignty and international diplomatic efforts. The ministry insisted that Eritrea has no territorial ambitions against Ethiopia and maintains a defensive military posture. The claims could not be independently verified. Eritrea Rejects Ethiopian Allegations The Eritrean government accused Ethiopia’s ruling Prosperity Party of pursuing policies that threaten regional stability, alleging that Addis Ababa has engaged in military pressure, diplomatic hostility and efforts to undermine Eritrean sovereignty. The statement rejected allegations that Eritrean forces had invaded Ethiopia or continued operating inside Ethiopian territory. It also disputed claims concerning areas covered by the 2002 Eritrea-Ethiopia Boundary Commission decision, arguing that some accusations of Eritrean military presence refer to territory awarded to Eritrea under that ruling. The competing territorial interpretations remain a central source of disagreement between the neighboring countries. Ethiopia has previously accused Eritrea of conducting military incursions and supporting armed opposition groups, allegations that Asmara denies. The latest Eritrean statement does not independently establish the location of forces operating near the border. Asmara Challenges International Calls for Restraint In a notable diplomatic position, Eritrea criticized international appeals urging both Ethiopia and Eritrea to de-escalate tensions. The ministry argued that calls directed equally at both governments overlook what it describes as Ethiopia’s responsibility for the confrontation. According to Asmara, diplomatic initiatives should focus on ending policies it considers threatening to Eritrean sovereignty rather than treating the two countries as equally responsible for the crisis. The position comes as international concern grows over the possibility of renewed conflict between the neighboring states. The United States and United Kingdom have called for restraint and diplomatic engagement. As previously detailed in Kulu Media’s coverage, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged de-escalation during discussions with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. The United Kingdom has also backed African Union mediation as regional tensions intensify. Sovereignty and Red Sea Dispute Eritrea’s statement also addressed the broader disagreement surrounding Ethiopia’s ambitions for access to the Red Sea. The ministry emphasized that Eritrean sovereignty and territorial integrity are non-negotiable, rejecting any attempt to justify territorial changes on economic or strategic grounds. Ethiopia, a landlocked country, has repeatedly emphasized the importance of securing reliable maritime access for its growing population and economy. However, disputes over the means of obtaining such access have contributed to deteriorating relations with Eritrea. Asmara maintained that it has no claims over Ethiopian territory and is committed to respecting internationally recognized boundaries. The ministry nevertheless warned that Eritrea remains prepared to defend its sovereignty against aggression. Growing Risk of Regional Conflict The latest statement follows weeks of deteriorating relations between Ethiopia and Eritrea, including diplomatic expulsions, accusations of military incursions and renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia. On October 1, Ethiopia announced the closure of its embassy in Asmara and the expulsion of Eritrean diplomats. Eritrea subsequently severed diplomatic relations with Ethiopia. The diplomatic breakdown has coincided with renewed military operations in Tigray, where Ethiopian federal forces and allied fighters have advanced through several areas previously controlled by TPLF-aligned forces. The confrontation has raised concerns about the possibility of a wider conflict involving the two countries. Kulu Media previously examined the growing war risk as military movements and competing accusations increased tensions near the border. In its October 21 statement, Eritrea maintained that sustainable regional peace requires respect for sovereignty, non-interference and internationally recognized boundaries. The government also rejected suggestions that it seeks a confrontation with Ethiopia. Despite the latest declaration, the central disagreements between Addis Ababa and Asmara remain unresolved. The immediate significance of the statement lies in Eritrea’s formal rejection of Ethiopia’s military allegations and its criticism of international diplomatic efforts that call on both governments to exercise restraint. With tensions already affecting Tigray and raising concerns across the Horn of Africa, the competing positions highlight the challenges facing efforts to prevent another major regional conflict. Published 2 days ago on October 21, 2026 By Kulu Media News Desk File Photo: Russian President Vladimir Putin shakes hands with US special envoy Steve Witkoff during a meeting in St. Petersburg, Russia. Credit: Sputnik / Pool / AFP-Jiji Russian President Vladimir Putin met US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Saint Petersburg on Wednesday, October 21, as Washington intensified diplomatic efforts to negotiate a ceasefire and end the war in Ukraine. During the meeting, Witkoff said there was a basis for reaching a ceasefire and urged Putin to consider restarting trilateral negotiations involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States, according to Russian news agencies Interfax and TASS, whose accounts were reported by Reuters . The American envoy proposed discussions involving technical experts from the three countries to address outstanding issues in a potential settlement. He also presented documents outlining Washington’s approach to ending the conflict. The discussions followed Witkoff’s meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and European representatives in Oslo on Tuesday, where participants examined proposals covering security guarantees, energy infrastructure and possible arrangements for a ceasefire. According to Associated Press , the latest diplomatic initiative seeks to revive negotiations that have struggled to produce a breakthrough despite repeated international efforts. Russia Signals Interest in Renewed US Relations Putin thanked US President Donald Trump for his efforts to negotiate an end to the conflict and expressed Russia’s interest in restoring economic relations with Washington, according to the Russian news agencies. The Kremlin also indicated its willingness to discuss wider international issues, including tensions involving Iran. The meeting took place amid concerns among Ukrainian officials and European allies about the direction of US policy toward Russia and the terms of a potential peace agreement. Although Witkoff expressed optimism about the possibility of renewed negotiations, Russia has not publicly accepted a new ceasefire framework or confirmed a date for trilateral talks. Prisoner Release Accompanies Diplomatic Talks The diplomatic meeting coincided with Russia’s release of American citizen Stephen Hubbard, who had been imprisoned after being accused of fighting alongside Ukrainian forces. Hubbard, a former teacher from Michigan, had been detained since 2022 and was sentenced in 2024 to nearly seven years in prison. The United States previously designated him as wrongfully detained. The diplomatic initiative also follows uncertainty over American military assistance, including a temporary interruption in intelligence sharing with Ukraine that was resolved earlier this month. According to Associated Press , President Trump had personally requested Hubbard’s release. The White House said the arrangement did not require the United States to release another prisoner in exchange. The release represented a concrete diplomatic gesture during the renewed engagement between Washington and Moscow, although it did not establish progress toward a broader settlement of the war. Fighting Continues Despite Diplomatic Efforts The latest negotiations come as Russian and Ukrainian forces continue military operations, including drone and missile attacks affecting civilian areas and energy infrastructure. Ukrainian authorities reported additional casualties and damage from overnight Russian strikes on October 21, underscoring the continuing humanitarian consequences of the conflict. Ukraine has repeatedly emphasized that any lasting settlement must include credible security guarantees and protect its sovereignty. Russia and Ukraine remain divided over territorial control and the conditions necessary for ending hostilities, making a comprehensive agreement difficult despite renewed American mediation. The latest meeting has reopened discussions about a possible ceasefire, but significant questions remain over whether Moscow and Kyiv can agree on its terms. For now, the proposed resumption of trilateral negotiations represents a diplomatic opportunity rather than a confirmed breakthrough in efforts to end the war. ethiopia.title: Kenya Red Cross Launches Emergency Response for Families Fleeing Moyale Clashes Into Marsabit
ethiopia.content: Kenya Red Cross Launches Emergency Response for Families Fleeing Moyale Clashes Into Marsabit - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Kenya Red Cross Launches Emergency Response for Families Fleeing Moyale Clashes Into Marsabit 23 October 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — The Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS) has launched an emergency response for families arriving in Moyale, in Kenya's Marsabit County, after fleeing insecurity linked to renewed clashes across the border in Ethiopia, as fighting in the disputed border town has forced civilians to seek safety on the Kenyan side. "Our priority is to make sure every family arriving in Moyale is safe, sheltered and treated with dignity," KRCS Secretary General Dr. Ahmed Idris said in a statement, adding that the organisation's staff and volunteers would continue responding as humanitarian needs evolve. The initial response is intended to reach 1,000 households, with KRCS teams working alongside the Marsabit County Government, national authorities and humanitarian partners to establish temporary shelters and distribute tents and essential household supplies, including blankets, sleeping mats, jerrycans and kitchen sets. The organisation is also providing Super Cereal, a fortified porridge flour intended to support the nutritional needs of young children and pregnant and breastfeeding women, as well as first aid for people requiring immediate assistance. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines A rapid needs assessment is underway to identify priority requirements, with early findings pointing to urgent needs for food, safe water, sanitation and hygiene services, primary health care and protection, particularly for women, children, older people and persons with disabilities. KRCS is also helping separated family members reconnect. The response follows renewed violence in Moyale, where clashes between security forces from Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regional states erupted on the morning of 22 October, following several days of escalating tensions over territorial and administrative disputes in the border town. The latest escalation followed a dispute over the opening of a Somali Regional State administrative office and the raising of its flag in Kebele 02, an area officials claim is administered by Oromia, a claim disputed by officials from the Somali region. The incident triggered an exchange of gunfire on 18 October, killing a 13-year-old girl, Diqqoo Jaataan Aagaa. Accounts differed over the circumstances of her death, with some attributing it to Somali regional forces and others saying she was caught in crossfire. Attempts by elders and security officials to defuse tensions, including an agreement to remove the flag, failed to secure a lasting resolution. Fighting subsequently spread to several localities in Moyale and parts of the wider East Borana Zone, while transport was disrupted, businesses closed and houses were reported burned. Security officials on both sides confirmed casualties and injuries but did not disclose figures. The full scale of the displacement and humanitarian needs remained unclear. The latest developments echo an earlier cross-border displacement crisis in March 2018 , when Kenyan authorities and humanitarian organisations received thousands of Ethiopians fleeing violence in Moyale after Ethiopian army personnel killed civilians in the town. At the time, KRCS said it had received at least 2,000 Ethiopian asylum seekers in the Kenyan border town following their displacement. The organisation distributed emergency family kits containing tarpaulins, kitchen sets, mosquito nets, soap, thermal blankets and jerrycans, while the Marsabit County Government provided food assistance. A medical unit was also deployed as authorities and humanitarian partners assessed needs among the arrivals, most of whom were women and children. ethiopia.content: Kenya launches emergency aid efforts as hundreds flee deadly clashes in Ethiopia For You News Faida Cafe Shows Radio TV Podcasts Live Events Search Kenya launches emergency aid efforts as hundreds flee deadly clashes in Ethiopia By Kenneth Gachie October 23, 2026 09:00 (EAT) Add as a Preferred Source on Google Follow us Follow on Whatsapp Follow on Google Follow on Twitter A file photo of Ethiopia's Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed . Audio By Vocalize The Kenya Red Cross Society has launched an emergency relief operation in Moyale, Marsabit County, to support families fleeing deadly clashes in neighbouring Ethiopia, with the initial response targeting 1,000 households in urgent need of assistance. In a statement on Thursday, the humanitarian organisation said the families had arrived in Kenya with few belongings and urgently needed shelter, food, safe water and healthcare as fighting continued across parts of southern Ethiopia. Red Cross teams are working with the Marsabit County Government, national authorities and partners to establish temporary shelters and distribute essential supplies, including tents, blankets, sleeping mats, jerrycans and kitchen sets. The organisation is also providing Super Cereal, a fortified porridge flour for young children, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers, as well as first aid to those requiring medical attention. In addition, the agency is helping family members who have been separated during the displacement reconnect through its family-links service. “Our priority is to make sure every family arriving in Moyale is safe, sheltered and treated with dignity. Our volunteers and staff are on the ground and will continue to respond as needs evolve,” said Secretary General Ahmed Idris. The families have fled fighting in Moyale, Ethiopia, where security forces from the Oromia and Somali regions clashed on Thursday amid rising tensions over a regional flag dispute. The violence erupted in Moyale on the Ethiopian side of the border following tensions over the display of the Somali Regional State flag at a local administrative office in an area administered by Ethiopia's Oromia Regional State. Oromia and the Somali Regional State are two of Ethiopia's federal regions, home predominantly to Oromo and ethnic Somali communities respectively. Both communities have longstanding ties to the border area. The killing of a 13-year-old girl on Oct. 18 further heightened tensions before armed confrontations rocked with heavy gunfire broke out Wednesday night and intensified Thursday. Residents reported heavy gunfire involving regional security forces, while local officials said the fighting had spread to Gumi Eldallo, Wachile and Arero districts in southern Ethiopia, according to Ethiopian local media stations. Homes and trading centers were burned, disrupting commercial activities and forcing residents to abandon their properties. The exact number of people killed or injured remained unclear, with no independently verified casualty figures available. Moyale, approximately 780 kilometers (485 miles) north of Kenya's capital, Nairobi, and about 770 kilometers (478 miles) south of Ethiopia's capital, Addis Ababa, by road, is a major commercial crossing between the two countries. The border town serves communities in both countries, with close family and trading connections making it an important route for people fleeing insecurity. During the visit, Abiy said Ethiopia must move beyond meeting its immediate economic needs and invest in scientific and technological development that would benefit future generations. "Ethiopia's next chapter is about transforming its immense potential and abundant natural resources into tangible development, technological advancement, and shared prosperity," Abiy said in a social media post following the visit. The prime minister stressed that reliable and sustainable energy was essential to industrialisation, manufacturing, digital infrastructure and broader economic development. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines He said nuclear technology offered Ethiopia an opportunity to strengthen its energy security while supporting scientific progress across several sectors. Beyond electricity generation, Abiy highlighted the potential applications of nuclear technology in healthcare, agriculture, industry and environmental protection, describing these fields as important areas for innovation and sustainable development. The Ethiopian Nuclear Energy Commission is responsible for establishing the institutional and technical foundations of the country's national nuclear energy programme. Abiy emphasised the importance of developing skilled professionals, strengthening scientific research and transferring technical knowledge to future generations. During the visit, the prime minister also spoke about Ethiopia's broader development ambitions, saying the country had a responsibility to lay the foundations for the advancement of Ethiopian civilisation. He said national development should not be limited to addressing immediate needs but should also focus on creating a lasting legacy for future generations across all sectors. The prime minister underscored the importance of ensuring that nuclear energy development proceeds peacefully, safely, responsibly and sustainably. Ethiopia's government views nuclear technology as part of its long-term efforts to expand energy capacity, strengthen scientific institutions and support economic transformation. The building, located on 9th Street, came down at approximately 1:00 p.m. local time. A ccording to an official statement from the National Construction Authority (NCA), the project was registered on July 30, 2025, under Land Reference Number 36/II/40. The developer on record is 9th Street Plaza Limited, and the contractor is Stromax Holdings E.A Limited. The registered professionals are Arch. Emmanuel Mwangi Maina and Eng. Joseph Muturi Mugu. Somalia’s Ambassador to Kenya, Jabril Ibrahim Abdulle, visited the scene and described the incident as a tragedy for the Somali community. He confirmed to the Somali National News Agency (SONNA) that lives had been lost and businesses destroyed, noting that the full extent of the damage to Somali-owned enterprises would only be known once rescue operations concluded. “This is a sad day that I share with the Somali community in Nairobi,” Ambassador Abdulle said, emphasizing that Eastleigh is home to a large Somali population whose livelihoods depend on the commercial activity in the area. A Commercial Hub in Ruins Eastleigh is not merely a residential neighbourhood; it is a densely packed commercial engine. The ground floor of the collapsed building had been rented out to an electronics shop, a butchery, and a grocery store, all of which were operating while construction continued on the upper floors. The destruction of these businesses represents an immediate loss of income for Somali traders and their families. The economic stakes are substantial. Somali investors have injected over $1.5 billion into Nairobi’s economy over the last two decades, according to the Kenya National Chamber of Commerce and Industry, as reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of Somali investment in Kenya . Eastleigh is the primary hub for much of that capital. The destruction of a building in this commercial zone represents not just a human tragedy but a significant blow to the economic ecosystem that connects Somali businesses in Nairobi to networks across East Africa and the diaspora. Witnesses described the chaos. Muhiyadin Abdi, a Somali shop owner whose business is adjacent to the collapsed structure, told AFP that he and others saw cracks forming and tried to warn people. “We saw the walls crumbling little by little for several minutes. We tried to scream, to warn people, but no one listened,” he said. “Then there was a huge noise, accompanied by a large cloud of dust. And the building collapsed.” Another resident noted that because the collapse occurred around the time of Friday prayers, many workers and shoppers were at the mosque, potentially reducing the death toll. However, engineering experts at the scene warned that many workers were still inside conducting finishing work, and that the number of trapped individuals could be significant. The Regulatory Failure Behind the Tragedy The collapse has exposed the dangerous regulatory environment that Somali businesses and residents navigate in Eastleigh. Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja confirmed that while the building had been approved for construction, it did not possess an occupation certificate. This means the businesses operating on the ground floor were doing so illegally, and the county government failed to enforce the law that would have kept them out of a construction site. “This building has no occupation certificate… this has potentially cost lives,” Sakaja said, acknowledging that lenient penalties for developers amount to a “slap on the wrist.” Experts point to a pattern of corner-cutting. John Ogallo, vice-president of the Institution of Engineers of Kenya, stated that distress signs, such as cracks, were observed before the collapse. “If you build with the wrong materials, it becomes a time bomb,” he warned. A report by the Kenya Institute for Public Policy Research and Analysis found that 86 buildings collapsed in Nairobi between 2009 and 2019, killing an estimated 200 people, with audits showing that the vast majority of buildings in the city fail to meet safety standards. What This Means for Somalia and Its Diaspora For Somalia, the Eastleigh disaster is a direct economic and human blow. The neighbourhood is the primary destination for Somali nationals traveling to Kenya for medical treatment, business, and education. It is also a critical node in the informal financial networks that connect the diaspora to the homeland. The destruction of businesses and the loss of life in this specific location will be felt deeply in Mogadishu and across Somali communities worldwide. The tragedy also underscores the vulnerability of Somali migrants and diaspora communities in Kenya. Many Somalis in Eastleigh operate in the informal economy, with limited access to formal insurance or legal recourse when disasters occur. The fact that the building was occupied illegally, with the tacit tolerance of county authorities, highlights a system where regulatory oversight is weakest in the very areas where Somali enterprise is most concentrated. The incident occurs against the backdrop of a complex but deepening bilateral relationship. As reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of Somalia-Kenya security talks , the two governments have been actively strengthening cooperation on security, trade, and cross-border movement. The reopening of border crossings and the push for a trade facilitation agreement have been central to this rapprochement. For the Somali community in Eastleigh, these diplomatic developments are not abstract. They determine the ease with which they can travel, trade, and access services in both countries. As rescue teams continue to dig through the rubble with excavators and improvised tools, the Somali government and community leaders will be watching closely. The response to this disaster, and the Kenyan government’s willingness to hold the developer and the county officials accountable, will determine whether Eastleigh’s residents can trust that the buildings they live and work in are safe. Critical Note The collapse of the 9th Street Plaza is not an accident. It is the predictable result of a construction boom in Nairobi that has outpaced the capacity and will of regulators to enforce safety standards. The NCA’s publication of the developer, contractor, and engineer names is a necessary step, but it is the bare minimum. The Governor’s admission that the building was occupied without a certificate, and his call for stronger enforcement powers, suggests that the county government knows the system is broken. For the Somali community, this is a moment of grief and anger. Ambassador Abdulle’s visit to the scene was appropriate, but it must be followed by concrete action. The Eastleigh tragedy is a reminder that the Somali diaspora’s economic success in Kenya, which has injected billions into the local economy, is built on foundations that are too often unsafe. Until the regulatory environment changes, the community will continue to bear the risks of a system that treats enforcement as optional. According to a statement from the Turkish Embassy in Mogadishu, the meeting focused on the common will to further enhance bilateral ties and friendly human connections. The discussions covered ongoing cooperation projects in energy, infrastructure, fisheries, security, health, education, space, and connectivity. The embassy thanked Prime Minister Barre for his reception and his support for Türkiye-Somalia friendship. The Prime Minister’s Office has previously expressed gratitude for Ankara’s role in rebuilding the Somali Armed Forces and modernising government institutions, highlighting the security dimension of the partnership [citation:10]. A Comprehensive Diplomatic Tour Wednesday’s meeting with the Prime Minister is part of a broader diplomatic tour Ambassador Alkan has undertaken since arriving in Mogadishu in September 2026. His engagement with Somali leadership has been extensive, signaling Ankara’s intent to maintain its deep footprint in the country. Ambassador Alkan began his tenure by presenting his credentials to President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud in early October, marking the start of his mission during the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries, as reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the credentials ceremony . He also visited the spaceport facility under construction in Warsheikh district, inspecting progress on a project that underscores the strategic and technological depth of the relationship, as detailed in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the visit . Beyond the executive branch, Alkan has engaged with security leadership. He recently met with the Somali Police Commissioner, Brigadier General Asad Osman Abdullahi, to discuss enhancing bilateral cooperation in the security sector, with a particular emphasis on advancing training programs and building the capacity of the Somali Police Force, especially the elite Haramcad unit, as noted in FTL Somalia’s coverage of police cooperation . In previous months, his predecessor, Alper Aktaş, held similar talks with the National Security Advisor and the Defence Minister, maintaining a consistent line of communication between Ankara and Mogadishu’s security apparatus. His diplomatic activity also extends to the legislative and informational branches. In May, the Turkish Embassy engaged with the Ministry of Information to develop frameworks for media modernization and cross-cultural exchange, as reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the information ministry talks . The Strategic Depth and Its Complications Türkiye’s relationship with Somalia is among the most comprehensive of any external actor. It spans humanitarian aid, infrastructure development, military training, and economic investment. Turkish firms operate Mogadishu’s port and airport, and the 2024 defense agreement has given Ankara a significant role in Somalia’s maritime security. However, this deepening engagement has not been without controversy. The federal government’s political opponents, including former South West State President Abdiaziz Laftagareen, have accused Türkiye of enabling a “clan-based agenda” through its military support, specifically citing F-16 airstrikes in the Baidoa region, as reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the complaint . The complaint adds a layer of political risk to Ankara’s military presence, entangling it in Somalia’s internal disputes. Critical Note Ambassador Alkan’s meeting with Prime Minister Barre is a routine diplomatic engagement, but the breadth of sectors discussed, from energy and fisheries to space and connectivity, reflects a relationship that has moved far beyond traditional aid. Türkiye is embedded in Somalia’s security architecture, its economic infrastructure, and even its technological ambitions. The diplomatic tour Alkan is conducting is a testament to the institutional depth of the relationship. He is not just meeting with the President and Prime Minister; he is engaging with the police, the information ministry, and visiting strategic projects like the spaceport. This is the behavior of an ambassador whose country has significant, long-term interests to protect. But the partnership’s intensity also carries risks. As the Laftagareen complaint demonstrates, Türkiye’s military role has made it a participant, willing or not, in Somalia’s internal political conflicts. The Somali government values Turkish support, but it also uses it as a shield against domestic and international criticism. The question for Ambassador Alkan is whether he can manage a relationship that is expanding in scope while navigating the political sensitivities that come with such deep involvement. The meeting on Wednesday was a reaffirmation of friendship. The challenge lies in what that friendship requires in practice. Dowladda Federaalka Galmudug Hiiraan News Jubaland News Koonfur Galbeed SSC Somaliland Follow us Search News Somalia Somalia faces risk of mass displacement as floods threaten hundreds of thousands Posted by: Horseed Staff About 874,000 people in Somalia could be forced from their homes over the next three months as heavy rainfall and rising river levels increase the risk of widespread flooding, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) has warned. 23 October, 2026 Share Tweet The warning comes as communities across the country continue to recover from prolonged drought and repeated displacement. The IOM said on Wednesday that the risk of flooding between October and December could leave hundreds of thousands of people without homes or livelihoods. The situation is being compounded by forecasts of above-average rainfall, as El Niño conditions are expected to intensify. “We are looking at the possibility of hundreds of thousands of people losing their homes in just a matter of weeks,” said Manuel Marques Pereira, the IOM’s chief of mission in Somalia. “Many of these families have already been displaced before and have very little left to fall back on.” Mr Marques Pereira said there was still an opportunity to reduce the impact of the floods, but warned that time was running out. “We urgently need funding to help people protect their homes and livelihoods, reach safer ground where necessary, and avoid another cycle of displacement,” he said. The warning has raised concerns over the prospect of people being forced to undertake dangerous journeys in search of safety, including across borders and by sea. Humanitarian organisations have also warned that climate-related disasters could further deepen Somalia’s existing humanitarian crisis, with the risk of severe food shortages and famine. Somalia has faced repeated droughts, floods and displacement in recent years, placing additional pressure on communities already struggling with limited access to food, water and basic services. El Niño occurs when sea surface temperatures rise in parts of the central and eastern Pacific Ocean. The phenomenon can disrupt atmospheric circulation and influence weather patterns around the world. Its effects vary from region to region. In some areas it can contribute to severe drought, while in others it can bring heavier rainfall and an increased risk of flooding. For Somalia, the immediate concern is that further flooding could force already vulnerable communities from their homes once again, adding to a cycle of displacement that humanitarian agencies are struggling to address. It covers the broader area of digital transactions, including electronic payment systems, digital currencies and financial transactions conducted through digital platforms, according to the ministry. The ministry said establishing clear rules for digital transactions would help support economic development while strengthening public confidence in digital financial services. Communications and Technology Minister Mohamed Adam Moalim, also known as Mohamed Soomaali, thanked MPs and the parliamentary committee on communications and technology for their work in reviewing and advancing the legislation. The two nations emphasized their commitment to Somalia's sovereignty, explicitly rejecting any diplomatic recognition of Somaliland as an independent entity. They reiterated that Somaliland is an integral part of the Federal Republic of Somalia and condemned any potential collaboration between Somaliland and Taiwan. Somalia views any direct agreements made by Somaliland with foreign entities as infringements on its sovereignty.

somalia.content: Somalia's Neighbor Signals Progress: Kenya Says Ebola Outbreak "Within Reach" of Ending - Somali News today Live Home Politics Security Elections More News Premium Economy & Business Education Entertainment & Lifestyle Environment & Climate Health International Relations Technology & Innovation Sports News By Region Nationwide Benadir Galmudug Hirshabelle Jubaland Puntland South West State Somaliland North Eastern State Resources Infographics Downloads Videos FAQ About Somalia Generic selectors Exact matches only Search in title Search in content Post Type Selectors Home Politics Security Elections More News Premium Economy & Business Education Entertainment & Lifestyle Environment & Climate Health International Relations Technology & Innovation Sports News By Region Nationwide Benadir Galmudug Hirshabelle Jubaland Puntland South West State Somaliland North Eastern State Resources Infographics Downloads Videos FAQ About Somalia Generic selectors Exact matches only Search in title Search in content Post Type Selectors Generic selectors Exact matches only Search in title Search in content Post Type Selectors Health Nationwide Somalia’s Neighbor Signals Progress: Kenya Says Ebola Outbreak “Within Reach” of Ending October 23, 2026 6 min read NAIROBI , Kenya’s Ministry of Health reported no new Ebola cases on Thursday, marking the 17th day since the country confirmed its first imported case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease, with all 135 contacts now traced and the first group of quarantined individuals preparing to return home this weekend. According to a press release signed by Director General Dr. Patrick Amoth, all 14 samples collected and tested from alerts across the country over the previous 24 hours returned negative results. The total number of confirmed cases remains nine, including the index patient who died on October 5. All cases belong to a single cluster, with no evidence of community transmission. The Ministry also confirmed that the 8th National Ebola Taskforce convened on Thursday, chaired by Principal Secretary for Public Health and Professional Standards Mary Muthoni, to review progress and strengthen the response. The taskforce reviewed surveillance, case management, isolation facilities, essential supplies, and resource mobilisation to sustain the gains made so far. The PS reiterated the government’s commitment to containing Ebola through a coordinated whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach. The eight patients currently receiving treatment in designated isolation facilities are stable and responding well to care. They comprise four family members and four healthcare workers who treated the index case. All Contacts Traced, No Quarantine Transmission The Ministry confirmed that all 135 contacts associated with the first case have been traced, both within Kenya and internationally, with relevant health authorities formally notified under the International Health Regulations. This represents a 100 percent tracing rate, up from the 99.3 percent reported earlier in the week. Epidemiological investigations have established that every confirmed case had close contact with the index patient between October 3 and October 5, before entering quarantine, and each developed symptoms within Ebola’s known incubation period of two to 21 days. No infections have been traced to transmission within quarantine facilities, where infection prevention and control measures have been strengthened. From Sunday, October 25, the first contacts who complete their 21-day monitoring period and remain in good health will be released from quarantine and reunited with their families. The Ministry urged communities to receive them warmly, stating that they have passed the full monitoring period without falling ill and cannot transmit the infection to anyone. What This Means for Somalia Kenya’s progress is welcome news for Somalia, whose primary transit hub for international travel and humanitarian logistics is Nairobi. An uncontrolled outbreak in Kenya would have immediate and severe consequences for Mogadishu. The fact that all nine cases remain linked to a single chain, with no community transmission and all contacts traced, suggests that Kenya’s containment measures have functioned as intended. But Kenya’s success also sharpens the contrast with Somalia’s own preparedness. As reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the outbreak , the Kenyan index patient transited through Uganda and flew to Nairobi without being detected at the airport. A similar case arriving in Mogadishu would encounter screening systems that a WHO assessment rated at 20 percent capacity, with no dedicated isolation areas and no biosecure transport. The country’s border defenses remain thin despite regional alert levels. Somalia has taken steps to strengthen its preparedness. In late September, IGAD and Somalia’s One Health line ministries completed a four-day joint mission in Mogadishu to develop a costed, time-bound Ebola preparedness and response workplan. The plan covers surveillance, early warning, laboratory systems, and health workforce development, with a focus on cross-border coordination and points-of-entry preparedness. Somalia also conducted a three-day national simulation exercise in September to test detection, verification, reporting, and response protocols for a suspected imported Ebola case. The exercise identified gaps in reporting lines, notification and referral pathways, points-of-entry arrangements, and public communication. Earlier in the crisis, Somalia moved quickly to quarantine citizens returning from the DRC as part of its initial containment efforts. However, the DRC outbreak continues to accelerate, with more than 9,000 confirmed cases and 4,500 deaths. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or specific treatment. The WHO has warned that chains of transmission remain undetected and that the virus is still ahead of the response. Somalia has continued to hold high-level coordination meetings, such as the one reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of national Ebola readiness , but systemic vulnerabilities persist. Critical Note Kenya’s handling of its first Ebola outbreak has been competent and transparent. The Ministry of Health has published regular updates, traced every contact, and kept the public informed without inducing panic. The decision to allow quarantined contacts to return home after 21 days is scientifically sound and socially responsible. The outbreak appears contained, and the government’s statement that the end is “within reach” is not premature. The existence of a standing National Ebola Taskforce, meeting for the eighth time and chaired by a principal secretary, is a detail that matters. It indicates that Kenya’s response is not improvised but institutionalized, with a dedicated command structure that reviews surveillance, supplies, and resource mobilisation on a regular basis. Somalia has held coordination meetings and developed a workplan with IGAD, but it does not have a comparable standing taskforce with the authority to direct resources and enforce protocols across the health system. But Somalia should not mistake Kenya’s success for its own safety. The same qualities that have allowed Kenya to contain its cluster, a functioning health ministry with laboratory capacity, trained personnel, and a coherent command structure, are precisely those that Somalia lacks. Kenya screened over 700,000 travelers at points of entry and tested 461 samples since May. Somalia’s airport screening capacity remains rated at 20 percent, and its isolation and transport infrastructure for suspected cases is largely absent. The window for Somalia to close these gaps is narrowing. Kenya’s cluster appears contained, but the DRC outbreak continues to accelerate, and the movement of people across East Africa is constant. The IGAD workplan and the national simulation exercise are necessary steps. They are not sufficient. The difference between Kenya and Somalia in this outbreak is not luck. It is institutional capacity. Until Somalia builds that capacity, its border defenses will remain a promise rather than a barrier. Studies show the full implementation of the AfCFTA would increase intra-African trade by 52 percent or by $450 billion by 2035, according to the World Bank. Photo credit: File | NMG By Luke Anami Correspondent in Nairobi, Kenya Nation Media Group Thank you for reading businessdailyafrica.com Show plans Somalia has officially become the 50th State Party to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), completing a series of protocol steps needed to be a part of commercial framework. Mogadishu formally deposited its instrument of ratification at the African Union headquarters in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia on September 4 last month but details of formal membership were confirmed this week. AfCFTA Secretary-General Wamkele Mene told an audience at the official opening of this year’s 26th Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (Comesa) Summit in Harare, Zimbabwe that Somalia will now start enjoying full rights in the deal. Related East Africa PRIME Somalia assesses EAC membership benefits, two years on Oct 18 - 4 min read Africa PRIME Inside EAC, Comesa plan to cut paperwork, fees on cross-border trade Oct 21 - 4 min read The move grants Somali businesses and investors preferential access to a continental market of over 1.4 billion consumers. “In terms of implementation of the AfCFTA, your excellences, as we speak today, 54 members of the African Union have signed the agreement establishing the AfCFTA,” said Mene. “50 members of the African Union have ratified it. Somalia is the most recent member of the African Union to ratify the agreement establishing the AfCFTA. We congratulate Somalia for being the 50th state party to the AfCFTA, which further strengthens Comesa's contribution to continental trade.” Somalia’s participation adds further momentum to the collective effort to deepen regional value chains, expand trade and build a more integrated and prosperous Africa. It joined the East African Community at the end of 2024, after also receiving formal nod on debt forgiveness by a various international lenders including the World Bank. Gamal Mohamed Hassan, Somalia’s Minister for Commerce and Industry, submitted the instrument of ratification in September following its approval by Parliament and presidential assent from President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. "Somalia's participation in the AfCFTA will create greater opportunities for local enterprises to access continental markets, attract foreign investment, diversify exports and participate effectively in regional value chains, supporting the country's broader economic development," said Hassan on Thursday. The government viewed the agreement as a platform to accelerate industrialisation, attract investment and drive economic growth, adding that the ministry would work closely with the private sector to maximise opportunities arising from membership. The ministry said its next priorities include aligning Somalia's tariff schedules with AfCFTA commitments, developing the required trade instruments and conducting nationwide outreach to help businesses, exporters, cooperatives and small and medium-sized enterprises prepare for implementation. The AfCFTA Secretariat welcomed Somalia and looks forward to supporting the country as it advances domestic implementation and creates opportunities for the Somali private sector to participate effectively in intra-African trade. Somalia is a member of the East African Community as well as Comesa, both of which are regional blocs that serve as the main anchors for an effective AfCFTA. “Our regional economic communities are the building blocks of the continental market. And in this regard, we value the collaboration with Comesa and other regional economic communities,” said Mene. Among the 21 member states of Comesa, the vast majority have ratified the agreement, including Kenya, Rwanda, Djibouti, Eswatini, Uganda, Egypt, Ethiopia, Zimbabwe, Tunisia, Mauritius, Malawi, Zambia, Burundi, Seychelles, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Comoros, Madagascar and, most recently, Somalia. The 50 ratifying nations include Ghana, Kenya, Rwanda, Niger and Chad in the initial group, followed by a broad coalition across the continent, with Comoros, Mozambique, Liberia, Madagascar and Somalia among the most recent members. The AfCFTA aims to boost intra-African trade by lowering trade barriers and establishing a unified framework for the seamless movement of goods and services across the continent. تصل معركة البقاء في دوري أبطال أفريقيا "توتال إنرجيز" لموسم 2026/2027 إلى مرحلة حاسمة في عطلة نهاية هذا الأسبوع؛ إذ تواجه أندية أفريقية عريقة خطر الإقصاء المبكر، بينما تسعى فرق طموحة لتحقيق مفاجآت مدوية وحجز مقاعدها في دور المجموعات. يتعين على أندية الترجي التونسي (بطل أفريقيا أربع مرات)، ومولودية الجزائر، وبترو أتلتيكو الأنغولي، تعويض خسائرها المؤلمة في مباريات الذهاب، وذلك خلال جولة الإياب من الدور التمهيدي الثاني، التي تُقام 15 مباراة منها في الفترة ما بين الجمعة 23 أكتوبر والأحد 25 أكتوبر 2026. كما يواجه حامل اللقب، ماميلودي صنداونز، اختباراً مصيرياً بعد تعادله سلبياً في مباراة الذهاب أمام فريق "ويليتي" الأنغولي، في حين يتوجب على تي بي مازيمبي -الفائز باللقب خمس مرات- تجاوز عقبة النادي الأفريقي التونسي للحفاظ على آماله القارية. وتأتي هذه الجولة الحاسمة بعد تأهل نادي "يانغ أفريكانز" التنزاني، الذي أصبح أول فريق يضمن مقعداً في دور المجموعات، عقب فوزه يوم الأربعاء على "سي إف إف إيه" ( CFFA ) من مدغشقر بنتيجة 4-1، ليحسم المواجهة لصالحه بنتيجة إجمالية بلغت 8-1. ومع تأهل "يانغ أفريكانز" بالفعل، تتبقى 15 مقعداً شاغراً في دور المجموعات، الذي من المقرر أن ينطلق في أواخر شهر نوفمبر. ومن بين أكثر المواجهات إثارة، يسعى الترجي التونسي لإنقاذ مسيرته في البطولة عندما يستضيف فريق "السويحلي" الليبي يوم السبت؛ حيث يمتلك الفريق الليبي أفضلية الفوز ذهاباً بنتيجة 1-0، ولا يفصله سوى 90 دقيقة عن تحقيق أحد أكبر الإنجازات في تاريخه القاري. وفي مواجهة صعبة أخرى، يستقبل مولودية الجزائر فريق "رينجرز إنترناشيونال" النيجيري يوم الجمعة، وهو مطالب بتعويض خسارته ذهاباً بهدفين نظيفين. وفي سياق مشابه، يواجه بترو أتلتيكو الأنغولي تحدياً كبيراً عند استضافته لفريق "سكوتلاند إف سي" الزيمبابوي، بعد أن انتهت مباراة الذهاب بخسارة الفريق الأنغولي بهدفين دون رد. يواجه فريق "صنداونز" اختباراً صعباً عندما يستضيف "ويليتي" في بريتوريا، وذلك بعد أن انتهت مباراة الذهاب في أنغولا بالتعادل السلبي (0-0). وفي تونس، تُقام مواجهة قوية أخرى يوم الأحد، حيث يستضيف "النادي الأفريقي" فريق "تي ​​بي مازيمبي" -الفائز باللقب الأفريقي خمس مرات- بعد أن تعادل الفريقان بنتيجة (1-1) في لوبومباشي. وبينما تواجه بعض الأندية العريقة ضغوطاً كبيرة، تسعى أندية أخرى لحسم تأهلها رسمياً بعد تقديمها أداءً قوياً في مباريات الذهاب. يدخل فريق "نهضة بركان" المغربي مباراة الإياب على أرضه يوم السبت متسلحاً بتقدمه (2-0) على "ستار سبورت أكاديمي" من سيراليون، بينما يسعى "الهلال" السوداني للحفاظ على تقدمه بنفس النتيجة أمام "بن سيداما " الإثيوبي يوم الأحد. كما يتمتع فريق "كولومب سبورتيف" الكاميروني بوضع مريح بعد تحقيقه فوزاً لافتاً خارج أرضه بنتيجة (2-0) على "تونغيث" السنغالي، مما يجعله على أعتاب التأهل لدور المجموعات. وقد تشهد المرحلة المقبلة حضوراً مزدوجاً لتنزانيا؛ إذ يُعد فريق "سيمبا" الأقرب للانضمام إلى "يانغ أفريكانز" بعد تحقيقه فوزاً ساحقاً بنتيجة (6-1) خارج دياره على "15 دي أغوستو" من غينيا الاستوائية يوم الأربعاء. وفي مصر، يسعى كل من "بيراميدز" و"الزمالك" لحسم التأهل على أرضهما يوم السبت، بعد أن حقق كلاهما الفوز بنتيجة (1-0) خارج الديار في جولة الذهاب، أمام "المريخ بنتيو" من جنوب السودان و"الجيش" الرواندي على التوالي. ويضع فريق "أورلاندو بايرتس" الجنوب أفريقي نفسه في موقف جيد بعد فوزه (1-0) خارج ملعبه على "أفريكان ستارز" الناميبي، رغم أنه سيحتاج إلى تقديم أداء منضبط مجدداً في مباراة الإياب. وفي سياق آخر، يأمل فريق "أسيك ميموزا" الإيفواري في استغلال عاملي الأرض والجمهور أمام "المغرب الفاسي" المغربي، بعد تعادلهما (1-1) في لقاء الذهاب. أما فريق "هورويا" الغيني فيسافر لمواجهة "المريخ" السوداني وهو متقدم بفارق ضئيل (1-0)، في حين يتعين على "نواذيبو" الموريتاني تعويض خسارته ذهاباً (2-1) أمام "سان بيدرو" الإيفواري. تشير الفوارق الضئيلة في العديد من هذه المواجهات إلى أن نتائج معارك التأهل لا تزال غير محسومة، مع احتمالية حدوث المزيد من المفاجآت في ظل سعي الأندية المستمر للبقاء في دائرة المنافسة على المجد القاري. وستنضم الأندية الـ 15 المتأهلة إلى فريق "يانغ أفريكانز" في دور المجموعات، الذي يضم 16 فريقاً، ضمن منافسات دوري أبطال أفريقيا "توتال إنرجيز" لموسم 2026/2027. دوري أبطال
